The spread of a new coronavirus from Wuhan, in central China, to the rest of the world in the winter of 2019 to 2020. The first known cases of a new pneumonia appeared in Wuhan in December 2019, many linked to a market selling seafood and live animals. Whether the virus passed from animals there or came from elsewhere is still argued.

China locked down Wuhan, a city of about 11 million, on 23 January 2020, but by then travellers had carried the virus abroad. In Europe it first took hold in northern Italy, where hospitals in Lombardy were overwhelmed in February and March, and Italy was the first European country to lock down nationwide. From there and from Iran it spread across Europe, the Middle East and the Americas.

On 11 March 2020 the World Health Organization declared a pandemic. The COVID-19 pandemic killed millions and shut down much of the world economy until vaccines arrived. Older pandemics moved along trade routes too, like the Black Death.
